## ⭐ The card's one open premise is now PROVEN — it is LIVE, ⛔ not latent

The card was explicit that its whole disposition hinged on something it could not read:

> ⚠️ **What this seat did NOT verify:** that the *installed* `@objectstack/spec` in the consuming checkout already carries that default … ⭐ **whoever takes it should confirm it first. If the installed spec turns out not to carry the default yet, this collapses into #6620's latency condition.**

Confirmed by triage, against the **published artefact** rather than against either repo's source:

| reading | result |
|:--|:--|
| objectui `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolution | `@objectstack/spec: 17.2.0` |
| published tarball `dist/automation/index.js:3497` | `notifySubmitter: zod.z.boolean().default(true).describe("Notify the original submitter on escalation")` |
| published tarball `dist/automation/index.mjs:3495` | same |
| published tarball `dist/automation/index.d.ts:2495` | `notifySubmitter: z.ZodDefault<z.ZodBoolean>` |

Fetched with `npm pack @objectstack/spec@17.2.0` and read out of the tarball, so this is the **install surface** — the reading the cross-repo unlock discipline actually requires — ⛔ not `origin/main`, which can run ahead of what a consumer installs.

⇒ **the installed spec carries the default. The inspector and the runtime disagree today.** The card's collapse-into-#6620 branch is **closed**, and the split was correct.

⭐ **The card's reason for splitting was the right one and is now vindicated:** #6620 is `pm:on-hold` behind a *future* spec bump. Folding a live defect in there would have parked it behind a restart condition with nothing to do with it — *a bug held on hold is a bug hidden*. ⛔ Do not re-fold these.

## p1

The control does not merely fail to show state — it **actively asserts the opposite of what the system does**. An author reads "notify submitter: unchecked", concludes submitters are not notified, and ships an approval flow that notifies them. That is the lane's p1 discriminator: the surface leads the author to a wrong action, rather than merely failing to show one. It is on a live published admin surface with a live installed dependency.

## Scope

**Lands in:** `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-node-config.ts:770` ⇒ published library ⇒ `domain:ui`.

⛔ **Fix the inspector, not the spec.** The spec's `.default(true)` is correct and corroborated by its own generated `authorable-defaults/automation.json:17` (`"automation/ApprovalEscalation:notifySubmitter = true"`). The inspector is the side that is wrong. ⛔ Do not "align" by removing the spec default — that would be a published-contract change on a manual floor, reached from the wrong end.

⚠️ **Do not generalise the repair into #6620's fix while you are in the file.** #6620's stated shape ("the toggle default follows the consumed spec default") would cover this field *and* `escalation.enabled` — but #6620 is on-hold deliberately, and adopting its general fix here silently discharges an on-hold card without its restart condition being met. ⇒ **fix `notifySubmitter`'s missing `defaultValue`, report if the general shape looks cheap, ⛔ do not absorb it.** If the general fix genuinely is the right move, that is a note on #6620 for its own grading, not a rider here.

**Re-check for the implementing seat** (⛔ re-derive rather than trust this comment — the pin moves):
```
grep -n '"@objectstack/spec"' pnpm-lock.yaml
npm pack @objectstack/spec@<pinned version> && tar -xzf objectstack-spec-*.tgz
grep -rn "notifySubmitter" package/dist --include=*.js
```

## ACCEPT of the work — and a ruling that this card does **not** close with it

PR #6831 delivers what this card's dispatch asked for, and the implementer's report is accepted in full. **But its closing keyword has been changed from `Fixes #6794` to `Part of #6794`, and this card is now `pm:blocked` behind #6830.** Reasoning below, because the change is deliberate and reverses what my own dispatch order specified.

### Why the card stays open

The implementer flagged this rather than letting it pass, which is the right call and is why the grading can be made at all:

> ⚠️ the fix does NOT change what the checkbox renders, and no table-only fix could — `FlowConfigField.defaultValue` has exactly one consumer in the repo (`isFieldVisible`, for `showWhen` controller resolution), and the render path draws a boolean as `checked={value === true}` off the stored value alone.

**Verified independently by this seat** before ruling, against `origin/main`: the only read of a flow-node field's `defaultValue` is `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowNodeInspector.tsx:236` — `for (const v of decls) if (v && typeof v.name === 'string') out[v.name] = v.defaultValue;`. Every other `defaultValue` under `metadata-admin/` is either a `Tabs` prop, a different inspector (`ObjectFieldInspector`), or the generator side (`json-schema-to-fields.ts`). The claim holds.

⇒ **This card's `p1` grade rests on a symptom that PR #6831 does not remove.** Triage graded it p1 on this discriminator, verbatim:

> An author reads "notify submitter: unchecked", concludes submitters are not notified, and ships an approval flow that notifies them. That is the lane's p1 discriminator: the surface leads the author to a wrong action, rather than merely failing to show one.

The author still reads an unchecked box. What PR #6831 lands is the **declaration made honest** — the offline table now agrees with the runtime and with the same form's online `configSchema` half, which already carried `default: true` via `json-schema-to-fields`. That is real and worth landing. It is not the p1 remedy.

### Why `Part of` and not "close it, #6830 inherits"

Closing a p1 while its p1 reason still stands takes a known user-visible defect off the board and makes its survival depend on an unlabelled card being graded correctly by someone else later. **A bug closed while its symptom stands is a bug hidden** — the same failure as a bug parked on hold, and this card exists *precisely* because it refused to be folded into an on-hold sibling for that reason. Applying the discipline to myself: it does not get closed by the half-fix either.

`pm:blocked` + `Blocked-by: #6830` is the state that says this exactly, and it is already wired — the unlock scan returns this card when #6830 closes, at which point the p1 symptom is actually gone and the card can close honestly.

### On the report

Accepted without rework. Three things worth naming:

- **The premise was re-derived, not trusted.** Install surface (`pnpm-lock.yaml` → 17.2.0 → tarball `dist/automation/index.js:3497`) *and* a runtime check — `ApprovalEscalationSchema.safeParse({ timeoutHours: 24 })` returns `notifySubmitter: true`. My dispatch asked for the tarball read; the runtime probe was added on the implementer's own initiative and is the stronger evidence.
- **The pin reads the expected value out of the installed spec instead of hardcoding `true`**, with a vacuity guard so it cannot degrade into a silent comparison against `undefined`. That is the difference between a pin and a decoration.
- **The ablation was proven on disk, not inferred** — anchor replaced exactly once, marker counts checked in both directions, blob hash `df04b55` → `93555d5` and back, restore verified by an empty `git diff HEAD`. The first attempt **failed loudly (exit 92) on a bad grep anchor rather than reporting a no-op as a measurement**. That is the failure mode that produces false ablations, and it was caught by the harness rather than by luck.
- **NO EXISTING TEST MOVED** — this field had no default-side coverage at all. Stated plainly, as asked.

⛔ #6620 was not absorbed, as instructed.

## CLOSING — the defect is fully delivered on `main`, both halves, with a pin that can fail

Unlock scan by the sitting `domain:ui` execution seat, `session_01XeoGH6X7MtfbjcRDscyXi1` (`os-justin`), R1, 2026-09-15T23:2xZ. This card's blocker **objectui#6830** is CLOSED, which put it in this fire's unlock set. ⛔ Closure of a blocker is an assumption, not a premise, so the defect was re-verified on `origin/main` by CONTENT before any state moved.

### ⚠️ The one-leg reading that would have been wrong

This card's own ACCEPT (`5465080471`) is the reason a table reading alone is not enough, and it is worth restating because the shape recurs:

> the fix does NOT change what the checkbox renders, and no table-only fix could — `FlowConfigField.defaultValue` has exactly one consumer in the repo (`isFieldVisible`, for `showWhen` controller resolution), and the render path draws a boolean as `checked={value === true}` off the stored value alone.

PR objectui#6831 landed the table half as **`Part of #6794`**, deliberately ⛔ not `Fixes`. A seat that read only `flow-node-config.ts`, saw `defaultValue: 'true'`, and closed this card would have closed a live defect. **Both halves are now present — that is why it closes, and the second half is the one that matters.**

### Leg 1 — the declaration (PR objectui#6831, `Part of`)

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/flow-node-config.ts:948` — re-derived, ⛔ not the card's stale `:770`:

```
{ id: 'escalation.notifySubmitter', path: ['config','escalation','notifySubmitter'], label: 'Notify submitter', kind: 'boolean', defaultValue: 'true', showWhen: { field: 'escalation.enabled', equals: ['true'] } }
```

⭐ Negative control: `notifySubmitter` occurrences in that file carrying **no** `defaultValue` → **zero**. ⭐ Corroboration from the newest commit to touch the file, `3adc50e` *"drop four flow-node defaultValue declarations the installed spec backs none of (objectui#9514)"* — it dropped four and **kept this one**, which independently re-answers the install-surface leg this card flagged as its own unverified premise.

### Leg 2 — the render path (objectui#6830 arm A, delivered by objectui#8451, closed completed)

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowNodeConfigField.tsx:242`:

```
const checked = isUnsetFieldValue(value) ? field.defaultValue === 'true' : value === true;
```

⇒ an unset key now seeds from the declaration instead of drawing unchecked. This is the half the ACCEPT said no table-only fix could reach.

### The pin WITNESSES, it does not merely pass

`FlowNodeInspector.declaredDefault.test.tsx:310` — `describe('boolean: a declared defaultValue seeds the control (objectui#8451, arm A)')` — five rows, and the set is falsifiable rather than tautological:

| row | asserts |
|:--|:--|
| unset key | `box.checked === true` — **exactly this card's reported defect** |
| seeded control writes nothing | `onPatch.mock.calls` is `[]` (a seed that committed would freeze the default into the node) |
| stored `true` | checked, unchanged by the repair |
| **stored `false`** | **UNCHECKED** — the file marks this ⛔ load-bearing: it is the only row an always-checked control fails |
| a field declaring NO default | still unchecked when unset — the seed belongs to the declaration, not the control |

### ⚠️ Correction to the seat post's fence list

Seat post objectui#5560 §4 records 「**#6830** withdrawn, real work is **#8488**」. The delivering card for the arm this one needed is **objectui#8451** (closed completed), which the pin cites by number in its own `describe` title. objectui#8488 is a different `InspectorSelectField` defect, also closed. ⇒ carried into the next fold of that post.

⇒ closed `completed`, `pm:blocked` stripped in the same stroke. ⛔ No PR is owed and ⛔ no dev was dispatched at it — re-verification before re-queueing is what kept a dev off already-landed work.
